newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish AP funds can't buy shares until '98 - report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish AP funds can't buy shares until '98 - report.

text.p: Sweden's public pension funds will not be allowed to buy shares until the second half of 1998, at the earliest, as a proposal to enable them to act on the bourse has been delayed, a weekly reported on Monday.
"The working hypothesis is to put forward a ministry memorandum this autumn," Goran Haag at the Finance Ministry told Veckans Affarer.
A proposal was previously expected before the summer.
The delay means a government bill cannot be presented before the beginning of 1998 and new regulations cannot take effect until mid-year 1998, at the earliest, the magazine said.
The five so called AP funds are expected to be allowed to together own a maximum of 25 percent of shares in a listed company.

Currently, three of the funds -- the so called first, second and third AP fund which together manage about 550 billion crowns -- are not allowed to buy shares, while the fourth and fifth AP fund have most of their around 60 billion crowns invested in shares.
A sixth AP fund has started this year and is mainly to invest in small and mid-sized companies.
